milano.title: Navigli canal-side loft with private terrace
milano.description_short: Designer one-bed loft on the Naviglio Grande, with private terrace and exposed brick walls. The most cinematic stretch of Milan's waterway.
milano.description_long:
On a quiet stretch of the Naviglio Grande, this one-bedroom loft occupies the upper floor of a sensitively restored 19th-century warehouse. The original masonry has been brought back, paired with a black steel staircase that signals the building's industrial provenance.

The living area runs the full width of the property, opening onto a south-facing terrace of 12 m² where the canal lies just beyond the parapet. A compact eat-in kitchen in dark oak and concrete sits at one end of the room; an integrated reading nook at the other.

Upstairs, a mezzanine bedroom enjoys vaulted ceilings and a clean en-suite bathroom finished in micro-cement. Storage has been thought through with care, including bespoke wardrobes and a service cupboard for laundry.

Navigli requires no introduction: aperitivo on the canal, the Saturday antique market and direct tram access to Duomo in twelve minutes. Porta Genova FS station is six minutes on foot.

A strong, characterful piece of inventory for a young professional, a pied-à-terre buyer or an investor targeting Milan's most photographed neighbourhood.

milano.title: Isola: bright two-bed steps from Bosco Verticale
milano.description_short: Recently refurbished two-bedroom apartment a short walk from Bosco Verticale and Gae Aulenti. The new face of Milanese urban living.
milano.description_long:
On a leafy street in Isola, this 78 m² apartment has just emerged from a full refurbishment and is offered turnkey. Floors are pale European oak; walls are smooth lime plaster in a warm neutral; ceiling heights of 3.05 m bring real volume to the space.

The living-kitchen runs across the south facade, opening through three full-height casement windows onto a private Juliet balcony. The kitchen is from an Italian boutique manufacturer, with quartzite tops and recessed handles. Both bedrooms enjoy quiet courtyard views; the principal accommodates a king bed with built-in storage.

A single full bathroom is clad in zellige tiles with a walk-in shower; a separate laundry room doubles as utility. Air-conditioning has been installed on all three exposures.

Isola has reinvented itself as a destination neighbourhood for Milan's creative class: Bosco Verticale, Piazza Gae Aulenti and the Saturday farmers' market on Via Borsieri are all within five minutes on foot. The M5 metro at Isola delivers Garibaldi in a single stop.

A confident entry into one of the city's most desirable neighbourhoods.

milano.title: Porta Romana: refurbished one-bed near the new Olympic Village
milano.description_short: Compact one-bedroom flat in a 1930s building, fully renovated, six minutes from Porta Romana M3 and the new Olympic Village development.
milano.description_long:
Set in a well-kept 1930s building with porter service, this 55 m² apartment has been redesigned around clarity and light. The architect has consolidated services into a single block, releasing a generous open-plan reception that captures the south-east light through original casements.

The kitchen is concealed within a sequence of full-height oak cabinetry; a stone-topped peninsula serves as informal dining. The bedroom, which sits on the quiet courtyard, can comfortably accommodate a king bed with bedside storage. A walk-in wardrobe links to the bathroom, finished in tadelakt and brushed nickel.

The building is one block from the new Olympic Village construction site (delivering late 2026): a clear catalyst for rental yield and resale value. Porta Romana M3 is six minutes on foot, with Duomo reachable in nine minutes.

Ideal entry point for an investor or a first-time premium buyer who values position, build quality and a recent renovation that does not need to be redone.

milano.title: Città Studi: three-bed family flat with courtyard garden
milano.description_short: Spacious three-bedroom apartment with private cellar in a 1950s building, steps from Politecnico and the Città Studi tram network.
milano.description_long:
On a quiet residential street in Città Studi, this 105 m² family apartment offers exactly what the market most lacks: real bedroom volume, a working eat-in kitchen and a sensible price per square metre for the postcode. The current owners have lived here for fifteen years; the apartment has been maintained carefully but invites a cosmetic refresh.

The entrance hall opens onto a double reception running north-south, with original parquet and a marble fireplace. The eat-in kitchen sits on the courtyard side; three bedrooms are arranged along the night corridor, the principal with a recently refitted en-suite shower room. A second family bathroom and a service balcony complete the floorplan.

The building is fitted with a passenger lift, a 24-hour porter and a planted internal courtyard. A private cellar of 6 m² is included in the sale.

Città Studi is Milan's quietest university village: tree-lined streets, the Politecnico and Bicocca campuses within walking distance and direct tram access to Duomo via the historic Line 9. Strong fundamentals for a family buyer or a buy-and-hold investor.

milano.title: Brera: piano nobile two-bed with frescoed ceilings
milano.description_short: Piano nobile two-bedroom in a Brera palazzo, with frescoed ceilings, herringbone parquet and views over the Pinacoteca rooftops.
milano.description_long:
On the piano nobile of a 19th-century palazzo a minute from the Pinacoteca, this 110 m² apartment is a textbook expression of Brera's gentle grandeur. Three bays of windows face Via Solferino; the rooflines of the Pinacoteca and the Botanical Garden are visible from the reception sofas.

Frescoed ceilings, restored in 2018, run across the principal reception and the formal dining room; both rooms are connected enfilade and finished with original herringbone parquet. The kitchen is a separate room, fitted by a Milanese maker in oak and Verde Alpi marble.

Two bedrooms occupy the quiet courtyard wing. The principal suite includes a fitted dressing room and an en-suite bathroom in honed travertine; the second bedroom shares the family bathroom finished in Vicenza stone.

The building is grand but discreet: gated entrance, a single resident per floor, lift and porter from 7am to 8pm. A private cellar is included in the sale; a single garage space is available separately by negotiation.

Brera at its most authentic: the Pinacoteca, the Botanical Garden, Antica Trattoria della Pesa and the Saturday market on Via San Marco are all within a five-minute radius.

milano.title: Cinque Vie: designer three-bed in a restored palazzo
milano.description_short: Recently restored three-bed apartment in Milan's design district, with double-aspect reception and walking distance to Duomo.
milano.description_long:
On a cobbled side street in the heart of the Cinque Vie design district, this 138 m² apartment occupies the second floor of a restored 17th-century palazzo. The renovation, completed by a Milanese studio in 2023, balances the building's historic shell with a contemporary, gallery-grade interior.

The entrance opens onto a double-aspect reception of generous proportions, with original wood beams overhead and wide-plank oak underfoot. A discrete open kitchen in matt black and Bianco Statuario marble is integrated into one end of the room, leaving the seating area uninterrupted by services.

Three bedrooms arranged in a private wing, the principal with a dressing area and en-suite bathroom in book-matched onyx. Two further bedrooms share a second bathroom finished in micro-cement. A guest cloakroom and a separate laundry complete the layout.

The Cinque Vie has emerged as the city's most concentrated cluster of design galleries, anchored by the annual Salone del Mobile fringe events. Piazza Affari, Duomo and the Sforza Castle are all within five minutes on foot.

A confident, design-forward proposition for a creative or international buyer.

milano.title: Sempione: park-facing three-bed with private balcony
milano.description_short: Three-bedroom park-facing apartment with private balcony, in a stately period building on Corso Sempione.
milano.description_long:
Set on the third floor of an elegant 1920s building, this 150 m² apartment enjoys a direct view onto Corso Sempione and, beyond, the Arco della Pace and Parco Sempione. The owners have lived here for two decades; the apartment is presented in excellent condition with a recent cosmetic refresh.

The living-dining room runs across the front facade, opening through three french windows onto a 9 m² balcony. The kitchen is a separate, fully fitted room finished in lacquered cabinetry. Three bedrooms occupy the quiet rear of the apartment; two bathrooms (one en-suite to the principal) are finished in marble and limestone respectively.

The building offers porter service, lift access, a leafy internal courtyard and a private cellar. Air-conditioning is installed throughout. A garage space is available separately by negotiation.

The Sempione axis is one of Milan's most desirable family addresses, anchored by the park, the Triennale Design Museum and the historic tram lines that thread through the neighbourhood. Cadorna FS and M1 are eight minutes on foot.

milano.title: Porta Nuova: contemporary three-bed with skyline views
milano.description_short: Three-bed contemporary apartment on a high floor near Piazza Gae Aulenti, with floor-to-ceiling glazing and concierge service.
milano.description_long:
On the fourteenth floor of one of Porta Nuova's signature residential towers, this 145 m² apartment delivers the prototype Milanese skyline experience: floor-to-ceiling glazing, double aspect over the Bosco Verticale and Garibaldi station, and a covered terrace of 18 m² where the city lights take care of the soundtrack.

The open-plan reception accommodates a formal dining area and a sequence of seating zones. The kitchen, by an Italian boutique brand, is finished in matt lacquer and quartzite. The principal suite includes a fitted dressing room and an en-suite bathroom in book-matched marble; two further bedrooms share a family bathroom in limestone.

The building offers 24-hour concierge, a residents-only gym, a courtyard garden and underground parking. The sale includes a single secure parking space and a basement cellar.

Piazza Gae Aulenti is two minutes on foot, with the Apple Store amphitheatre and the Saturday farmers' market beneath the apartment windows. M5 Isola and Garibaldi FS are within a five-minute radius.

A turnkey proposition for the international buyer who wants Milan's newest skyline at street level.

milano.title: Quadrilatero: trophy piano nobile on Via Sant'Andrea
milano.description_short: Piano nobile trophy apartment of 380 m² with three exposures, a private garden courtyard and bespoke restoration on Via Sant'Andrea.
milano.description_long:
An exceptionally rare offering on Via Sant'Andrea, this 380 m² piano nobile apartment occupies the principal floor of an 18th-century palazzo whose neighbours are the city's most established couture houses. The owner has just concluded a six-year restoration with a leading Milanese architect, returning the apartment to its full Belle Époque proportions while inserting a discreet, museum-grade contemporary infrastructure.

The enfilade of three reception rooms runs along the south facade, each with restored frescoed ceilings, original chevron parquet and double-doors clad in burr walnut. A formal dining room of 50 m² connects to a service kitchen finished in lacquered cabinetry and Calacatta marble.

The night wing comprises four bedroom suites, each en-suite, with the principal occupying a dedicated 80 m² volume that includes a sitting room, two dressing rooms and a bathroom in book-matched onyx with a freestanding bath at the centre of the floor.

The apartment uniquely enjoys a 90 m² private garden courtyard, planted with mature magnolia and accessed via a glazed loggia from the main reception. Building amenities include 24-hour porter, lift access from the resident garage and a dedicated cellar.

A defining piece of inventory for the international buyer seeking a primary residence on Milan's most prestigious shopping street.

milano.title: Magenta: detached villa with garden, pool and garage
milano.description_short: A rare detached villa within the city boundary, with private garden, infinity pool and four-car underground garage near Sant'Ambrogio.
milano.description_long:
In a city where detached residences are vanishingly rare, this 460 m² villa offers a complete proposition: full plot, private garden, infinity pool and four-car underground garage, all within a five-minute walk of Sant'Ambrogio M2 and Parco Sempione.

The villa was rebuilt to the foundations in 2019 by a leading Milanese studio. Behind the sympathetic Liberty-era facade, the interior is wholly contemporary: a triple-aspect main reception runs across the garden side, with sliding panels of two-metre-tall glass that disappear into the wall, opening the entire ground floor onto the planted garden and pool deck.

The living level includes a sculptural staircase in Carrara marble, a formal dining room and an open kitchen by an Italian boutique maker. A study, guest cloakroom and laundry complete the level.

On the first floor, four bedroom suites are arranged with absolute privacy. The principal occupies a dedicated wing with a 30 m² dressing room and a marble bathroom with private terrace overlooking the garden.

A wellness level beneath includes a 12-metre infinity pool, hammam, gym and direct access to the four-car garage. A rare opportunity to acquire a freestanding asset of this calibre within the historic city perimeter.

mallorca.title: Palma Old Town: one-bed pied-à-terre with rooftop access
mallorca.description_short: A characterful one-bed apartment in a restored 18th-century building in the heart of Palma's old town, with access to a shared rooftop overlooking the cathedral.
mallorca.description_long:
A discreet doorway on Calle Apuntadores opens onto the foyer of a 1740s townhouse, sensitively restored in 2022. On the second floor, this one-bedroom apartment of 58 m² balances original stone walls and exposed beams with a quiet, contemporary interior in lime plaster and pale European oak.

The living-kitchen is double-aspect, capturing morning sun from the front and the afternoon shadow of the cathedral from the side. The bedroom enjoys a vaulted ceiling and built-in wardrobes; the bathroom is finished in honed limestone with a rainfall shower.

The building offers a shared rooftop terrace, accessed from a discreet lift, where loungers and a small herb garden capture the unbroken view of Palma cathedral and the bay beyond.

La Lonja, Plaza Mayor and the new wave of Palma's design hotels and natural-wine bars are all within a three-minute radius. The marina is six minutes on foot; Palma airport delivers central Europe in two hours.

A strong pied-à-terre or boutique rental asset in a market that continues to compress.

mallorca.title: Portixol: two-bed sea-front with morning sun
mallorca.description_short: Sea-front two-bed apartment in the heart of Portixol's restaurant strip, with a sun-trap balcony and direct view onto the marina.
mallorca.description_long:
Portixol has, over the last decade, completed its transformation from working fishermen's village to one of Europe's most relaxed waterfront neighbourhoods. This second-floor apartment sits at the centre of that change: 72 m², two bedrooms, one bathroom and a south-east-facing 8 m² balcony where the boats of the marina are framed between two palm trees.

The living-kitchen is open-plan, with light pouring through the front facade from sunrise. The kitchen is contemporary, fitted with a stone-topped peninsula. The principal bedroom enjoys a partial sea view; the second is currently configured as a study and works equally well as a guest room.

The bathroom is finished in tadelakt with a walk-in shower and matt black fittings. Air-conditioning is installed throughout.

The promenade beneath the apartment leads, in a fifteen-minute walk, into Palma's old town along the seafront. Cala Estancia and Portixol's surfable beach are immediately to the east. A rental-strong asset with credible long-term appreciation in one of the island's most stable neighbourhoods.

mallorca.title: Sóller: three-bed townhouse in the orange-grove valley
mallorca.description_short: A traditional Mallorcan townhouse in the centre of Sóller, with three bedrooms, original terracotta floors and a small interior courtyard.
mallorca.description_long:
Set on Carrer de la Lluna, the artery of Sóller's old town, this three-bedroom townhouse offers a generous 118 m² distributed over three floors. The current owners have lived here for twelve years; the property is in good condition but invites a cosmetic refresh by a sensitive buyer.

The ground floor opens onto a stone-floored entrance hall, a 24 m² sitting room with the original fireplace and a south-facing dining room that overlooks a small interior courtyard of 9 m². The kitchen is functional and well-fitted, with potential to integrate with the courtyard for a full indoor-outdoor configuration.

Upstairs, three bedrooms are arranged on the first floor, the principal with original beamed ceilings. A single full bathroom serves the level. The top floor is currently used as a multi-purpose room and includes a private roof terrace of 18 m² with views over the church bell tower and the Tramuntana ridges.

Sóller offers a year-round community, weekly markets, the historic narrow-gauge tram down to the port and a forty-minute drive into Palma. A characterful, honest piece of inventory for the buyer prepared to embrace a village rather than a resort.

mallorca.title: Santa Catalina: design two-bed with private patio
mallorca.description_short: Designer two-bedroom apartment in Santa Catalina, with private 12 m² patio and the Mercat de Santa Catalina at the doorstep.
mallorca.description_long:
Santa Catalina has, in the last decade, become Palma's most reliably interesting neighbourhood: a working market, a concentration of small restaurants and natural-wine bars, and a residential fabric of late-19th-century townhouses that lend themselves to careful conversion.

This ground-floor 84 m² apartment is one such conversion, completed in 2024 by a small Palma studio. The interior is finished in lime plaster, terracotta tiles and pale European oak; the original stone walls have been retained at the rear of the property and exposed on the patio side.

The living-kitchen runs across the full depth of the apartment, opening through two sets of french doors onto a private patio of 12 m². The patio is north-facing, planted with lemon and bougainvillea, and offers shade through the hottest part of the day.

Both bedrooms enjoy quiet exposures; the principal includes a fitted dressing area and an en-suite shower room finished in tadelakt. A second bathroom and a discreet utility complete the layout.

The Mercat de Santa Catalina is three minutes on foot; Palma cathedral is twelve minutes along the seafront.

mallorca.address_approx: Carretera de Cala Sant Vicenç, Pollença
mallorca.title: Pollença: restored stone finca with pool and olive grove
mallorca.description_short: Sympathetically restored stone finca of 180 m² on a 4,000 m² olive grove plot, with private pool and Tramuntana views.
mallorca.description_long:
Set on a 4,000 m² plot of mature olive trees five minutes' drive from Pollença's old town, this restored stone finca offers the prototype northern-Mallorca experience: cicadas, dry stone walls, a long evening light and the quiet bulk of the Tramuntana to the west.

The finca, originally built in the late 19th century, was fully restored in 2021. The interior is finished in lime plaster over original stone walls, with restored chestnut beams and reclaimed Mallorquin terracotta floors. The principal living-dining room runs across the south facade, opening onto a deep covered porch where the table seats ten.

The kitchen is a separate, working room finished in cream cabinetry and a marble-topped island. Three double bedrooms are arranged on the ground floor; the principal includes a dressing area and an en-suite shower room. A second family bathroom serves the remaining two.

Outside, a 10-metre saltwater pool sits on a terraced lawn surrounded by mature olive and almond trees. A pool house with summer kitchen and shower extends the entertaining footprint. Solar panels, a wood-burning fire and high-grade insulation deliver a low running cost across the year.

A confident, honest piece of inventory for the buyer who wants a genuine finca experience without a five-year project.

mallorca.title: Portals Nous: marina-front three-bed with private terrace
mallorca.description_short: Three-bedroom apartment with 40 m² terrace overlooking Puerto Portals marina, in a 24-hour security complex with pool and gym.
mallorca.description_long:
On a high floor of a prestigious 1990s residential complex directly above Puerto Portals, this 165 m² apartment delivers the most photographed sea view in south-west Mallorca: the full sweep of the marina, the Bay of Palma and, on a clear day, the cathedral spires in the distance.

The apartment has been fully refurbished in 2022. The 40 m² south-west-facing terrace runs along the full length of the reception, configured for both lunch and dining. The reception is open-plan with a contemporary kitchen in lacquered cabinetry and Calacatta marble. Three bedrooms are arranged in a private wing; the principal includes a dressing room and en-suite bathroom in book-matched marble.

The complex offers 24-hour security, a heated outdoor pool, residents-only gym, manicured gardens and underground parking. A single secure parking space is included.

Puerto Portals offers a year-round community, a concentration of the island's most established restaurants and a deep-water marina that accommodates 50 m+ yachts. Palma airport is twelve minutes by car.

A confident proposition for the international buyer seeking turnkey marina-front living without the commitment of a full villa.

mallorca.title: Son Vida: contemporary villa with infinity pool
mallorca.description_short: Contemporary four-bedroom villa on a 1,800 m² plot in Son Vida, with infinity pool and city-and-sea panoramic views.
mallorca.description_long:
On a south-east-facing plot of 1,800 m² in the gated community of Son Vida, this 350 m² contemporary villa was completed in 2020 to a brief that prioritised volume, light and view. Three golf courses sit within walking distance; Palma cathedral is visible in the middle distance.

The ground floor is configured around a triple-aspect open-plan living-dining-kitchen of 90 m², with sliding glazing that retracts entirely to open the room onto a covered terrace and a 14-metre infinity pool. The kitchen is fitted by an Italian boutique maker, finished in matt lacquer and Calacatta marble.

The principal bedroom suite occupies a dedicated wing of the ground floor, with a private terrace, a dressing room and an en-suite bathroom in honed travertine. The first floor accommodates three further bedroom suites, each en-suite, all with terrace access and partial sea views.

The lower-ground level offers a wellness suite (hammam, sauna and gym), a two-car garage and a service kitchen for staff. The plot is landscaped with mature olives, almonds and a planted edible garden.

A confident, light-filled villa in one of the island's most established gated communities.

mallorca.title: Valldemossa: stone village house with terraced garden
mallorca.description_short: Sensitively restored 17th-century stone house in the heart of Valldemossa, with terraced garden and mountain views.
mallorca.description_long:
Set on a lane that climbs from the cobbled centre of Valldemossa, this 195 m² stone house was restored in 2019 by a Mallorcan architect with a brief to restore rather than renovate. The original stone walls, chestnut beams and reclaimed clay floors have been kept; the contemporary intervention is limited to discreet glazing, integrated lighting and a single kitchen-and-bathroom block.

The ground floor opens onto a stone-walled entrance hall, a 32 m² sitting room with the original Mallorquin fireplace and an open kitchen finished in cream cabinetry and a stone-topped peninsula. The first floor accommodates the principal bedroom with an en-suite shower room and a small private terrace overlooking the village.

The second floor includes two further bedrooms and a family bathroom finished in honed limestone. A dedicated study with vaulted ceilings occupies the converted attic.

Outside, a terraced garden of 140 m² is planted with lavender, rosemary, and a single mature olive. A discreet plunge pool of 3 by 6 metres has been integrated into the lower terrace, with stone seating and an outdoor kitchen.

Valldemossa offers a year-round community, the Cartoixa monastery and direct access to the GR-221 walking route. A piece of inventory for the buyer who values quietness over visibility.

mallorca.title: Port d'Andratx: cliff villa with infinity edge over the bay
mallorca.description_short: Contemporary cliff villa of 520 m² above Port d'Andratx, with infinity pool, private cinema and direct sea view to the bay entrance.
mallorca.description_long:
On a south-west-facing cliff plot of 2,200 m² above Port d'Andratx, this contemporary villa was delivered in 2022 by an internationally recognised studio. The architecture is intentionally horizontal, three offset volumes that step down the cliff and direct every principal view to the bay entrance and the open Mediterranean beyond.

The entrance level opens onto an open-plan reception of 130 m², with retractable glazing that disappears entirely into the structural walls. The kitchen, by an Italian boutique maker, is finished in matt black lacquer, Calacatta marble and bronze detailing.

Five bedroom suites occupy the lower two levels, each en-suite, each with sea-view terraces. The principal suite includes a dedicated sitting room, double dressing rooms and a marble bathroom that opens onto a private plunge pool.

Wellness amenities include a 22-metre infinity pool with submerged sun loungers, an indoor heated pool, hammam, sauna, fitness studio and a 14-seat private cinema. A four-car garage and dedicated staff accommodation complete the brief.

The villa is delivered fully turnkey, including bespoke interior design and a curated furniture package. A trophy proposition for the international buyer seeking a primary or holiday residence at the heart of Mallorca's most prestigious bay.

mallorca.title: Deià: stone waterfront villa with private cove access
mallorca.description_short: Restored stone villa of 410 m² on a 3,500 m² plot above Cala Deià, with private path to the cove and panoramic Tramuntana views.
mallorca.description_long:
On a south-facing terrace above Cala Deià, this 410 m² stone villa occupies one of the most coveted positions on Mallorca's west coast. The plot of 3,500 m² descends in landscaped terraces to a private gate that opens onto the path to Cala Deià beach, six minutes on foot.

The villa was restored in 2018 by a leading Mallorcan studio. The original stone walls, chestnut beams and clay tile floors have been retained; the contemporary intervention has been concentrated in the kitchen, bathrooms and an extended south-facing reception that opens entirely onto a covered terrace.

Four bedroom suites are arranged across two floors. The principal occupies the western wing of the upper floor, with private terrace, dressing room and a stone-clad en-suite bathroom that overlooks the bay. Three further bedroom suites enjoy a mix of mountain and sea views.

A 14-metre saltwater pool sits on the principal terrace, surrounded by mature olive, almond and citrus trees. A pool house with summer kitchen and outdoor shower extends the entertaining footprint. A two-car covered garage and a separate staff studio of 32 m² complete the brief.

Deià remains one of the Mediterranean's most rarefied villages, anchored by Belmond's La Residencia and the year-round community of artists and writers. A defining piece of inventory for the buyer who values discretion above all.

london.title: Shad Thames: warehouse one-bed with river view
london.description_short: Converted warehouse one-bedroom apartment in Shad Thames, with Thames-facing window and direct walk to Tower Bridge.
london.description_long:
Within a 19th-century spice warehouse converted in the early 1990s, this 52 m² one-bedroom apartment occupies a corner of the third floor, with a full-height Crittall window facing directly onto the Thames and Tower Bridge in the middle distance.

The living-kitchen runs the full depth of the apartment, with the original cast-iron columns and exposed brick walls retained. The kitchen, refurbished in 2023, is finished in matt black cabinetry and a quartzite-topped peninsula. The bedroom, with built-in oak wardrobes, enjoys a quiet courtyard exposure; the bathroom is recently refitted in honed travertine with a walk-in shower.

Building amenities include a 24-hour porter, secure cycle storage and a riverside courtyard. London Bridge station is six minutes on foot, delivering the City in two stops and Canary Wharf in eight via the Jubilee Line.

Shad Thames offers a working community of restaurants, design galleries (the Design Museum sits at one end of the strip) and a riverside walk that connects to Borough Market in fifteen minutes.

A characterful entry into Zone 1 ownership for a first-time premium buyer or an investor seeking a high-quality short-let asset.

london.title: Islington: Georgian garden-flat with private patio
london.description_short: Garden-floor two-bedroom apartment in a Georgian terrace off Upper Street, with private 8 m² patio and original cornicing.
london.description_long:
On a tree-lined Georgian terrace fifty yards from Upper Street, this 78 m² garden-floor apartment occupies the lower-ground and patio of a Grade II-listed property. The conversion has been sensitive: original cornicing, restored sash windows and a classic black-and-white encaustic tile floor in the entrance hall.

The living-dining room of 28 m² runs the full width of the apartment at the rear, opening through french doors onto a private patio of 8 m². The patio is east-facing, planted with established ferns and bamboo, and offers genuine privacy from the neighbouring gardens.

The kitchen is fitted in cream Shaker-style cabinetry with a stone-topped peninsula. Two bedrooms occupy the front of the apartment; the principal accommodates a king bed with built-in wardrobes, while the second is currently configured as a study. A single full bathroom is finished in honed marble.

The building shares a freehold; the apartment includes a 999-year lease, a residents-association car-share access and direct entry to Cross Street.

Upper Street, Camden Passage antique market and Highbury & Islington station are all within a five-minute radius. A confident entry into one of Zone 1's most reliably appreciating residential addresses.

london.title: Canada Water: new-build two-bed with dock view
london.description_short: Two-bedroom new-build apartment on Canada Dock, with private balcony, residents' gym and 24-hour concierge.
london.description_long:
On the eighth floor of a 2023-completed residential tower facing Canada Dock, this 70 m² two-bedroom apartment is offered with a balance of the developer's ten-year build warranty and a current EPC rating of A.

The living-kitchen runs across the south-east facade, with floor-to-ceiling glazing that opens onto a 6 m² private balcony with direct view onto the dock and the Canary Wharf skyline beyond. The kitchen is fully integrated, finished in matt grey lacquer and a stone-topped peninsula; the appliances are by a German premium brand.

Both bedrooms enjoy fitted wardrobes; the principal includes an en-suite shower room finished in marble-effect porcelain. A second family bathroom and a discreet utility cupboard complete the layout. Underfloor heating and mechanical ventilation with heat recovery (MVHR) are installed throughout.

The building offers a 24-hour concierge, residents-only gym, communal landscaped roof terrace, secure cycle storage and a single allocated underground parking space.

Canada Water Underground station (Jubilee, Overground) is six minutes on foot. Canary Wharf is reachable in four minutes, the City in twelve. A turnkey new-build asset for the buyer who values low maintenance and high transport connectivity.

london.title: Fulham: Victorian three-bed family house with garden
london.description_short: Three-bedroom Victorian terraced house with 28 m² rear garden, off Bishop's Park, in a recognised primary school catchment.
london.description_long:
On a quiet residential street five minutes' walk from Bishop's Park, this 108 m² Victorian terraced house offers a complete family proposition in Fulham's most desirable school catchment.

The ground floor opens onto a classic double reception of 36 m², with restored sash windows, original cornicing and a wood-burning fireplace at one end. The room flows into a rear kitchen-dining that extends through a 2015 side-return extension; french doors open onto a private 28 m² west-facing garden.

The first floor accommodates the principal bedroom (accommodating a king bed) and a second double bedroom, sharing a recently refitted family bathroom in honed limestone. The second floor accommodates a third bedroom and a studio room currently used as a home office.

The property is freehold, with EPC C and the gas central heating boiler replaced in 2022. The owners have lived here for nine years; the house is presented in good condition, with potential for a loft conversion (subject to planning) that could deliver a fourth bedroom.

Putney Bridge Underground (District Line) is six minutes on foot; the Thames Path runs along the southern edge of Bishop's Park. A confident, honest piece of family inventory in a market that continues to compress on supply.

london.title: Marylebone: mansion-block two-bed with porter
london.description_short: Two-bedroom mansion-block apartment off Marylebone High Street, with original parquet, porter service and 24-hour caretaker.
london.description_long:
On the third floor of a celebrated Edwardian mansion block off Marylebone High Street, this 95 m² apartment is presented in excellent condition following a 2023 refurbishment that respected the building's original detail. The reception is double-aspect, with restored herringbone parquet, original cornicing and full-height casement windows that face onto a quiet residential street.

The kitchen is a separate, fully fitted room finished in cream cabinetry and a quartz-topped peninsula. Two bedrooms occupy the rear of the apartment; the principal accommodates a king bed with bespoke fitted wardrobes and an en-suite shower room in honed limestone. A second family bathroom serves the smaller bedroom.

The mansion block offers a 24-hour caretaker, lift access, secure cycle storage and a planted communal courtyard. The lease is 989 years remaining; the service charge and ground rent are presented as moderate for the postcode.

Marylebone High Street, the Wallace Collection and Regent's Park are all within a five-minute walk. Bond Street (Elizabeth Line, Central, Jubilee) is six minutes on foot.

A confident, traditional piece of Marylebone inventory for a downsizer, a pied-à-terre buyer or an international owner seeking a low-maintenance Zone 1 asset.

london.title: Notting Hill: cobbled mews three-bed with garage
london.description_short: Three-bedroom mews house on a private cobbled lane, with integral garage, roof terrace and walk to Portobello Road.
london.description_long:
On a private cobbled mews lane off Hippodrome Place, this 130 m² mews house offers a freehold proposition rare to the postcode: three bedrooms, integral garage and a 14 m² roof terrace with views over the Notting Hill rooftops.

The ground floor accommodates the integral garage, a utility cupboard and a guest bedroom currently configured as a media room. The first floor is configured as the principal living level: an open-plan kitchen-dining-living of 42 m² that runs the full footprint of the house, with skylight glazing over the kitchen and french doors opening onto a small Juliet balcony.

The second floor accommodates the principal bedroom with an en-suite shower room and a substantial bespoke dressing area, plus a second double bedroom and a family bathroom finished in honed marble.

A staircase from the second floor leads up to a private 14 m² roof terrace, professionally landscaped with low planters, an outdoor shower and seating for six.

The property is freehold, with a 2018 full refurbishment by a recognised Notting Hill studio. EPC C; gas central heating; air-conditioning to the principal bedroom and living level.

Portobello Road market, the Electric Cinema and Holland Park are all within a five-minute walk. Notting Hill Gate Underground is seven minutes on foot.

london.title: Clerkenwell: warehouse loft two-bed with private terrace
london.description_short: Spectacular two-bedroom warehouse loft of 138 m² with private terrace, in a converted industrial building on St John Street.
london.description_long:
On the top floor of a sensitively converted late-Victorian warehouse on St John Street, this 138 m² duplex loft offers the prototype Clerkenwell live-work proposition: double-height ceilings, exposed steel structure, original brick walls and a private south-west-facing terrace of 16 m² accessed via an external steel staircase.

The lower level is configured as a continuous open-plan reception of 70 m², with full-height steel-framed glazing across the south facade and a separated kitchen-dining zone at one end. The kitchen is finished in matt black cabinetry, Calacatta marble and brushed brass; the reception is centred on a wood-burning stove.

A cantilevered steel staircase rises to a mezzanine bedroom floor, where the principal bedroom enjoys vaulted ceilings, a bespoke walk-in dressing room and an en-suite bathroom finished in honed limestone. A second bedroom and a family shower room complete the floor.

The building offers a 24-hour caretaker, secure cycle storage and a planted communal roof terrace separate from the apartment's private terrace.

Farringdon (Elizabeth Line, Thameslink, Circle, Hammersmith, Metropolitan) is six minutes on foot, delivering Canary Wharf in twelve minutes and Heathrow in thirty. Exmouth Market and Smithfield are both within five minutes.

A design-forward proposition for the creative or international buyer who values architectural character.

london.title: Hampstead: Victorian four-bed family house with garden
london.description_short: Four-bedroom Victorian semi-detached family house with 60 m² south-facing garden, a short walk from Hampstead Heath.
london.description_long:
On a tree-lined street one minute from the southern edge of Hampstead Heath, this 175 m² Victorian semi-detached family house has been carefully extended by the current owners and is presented in excellent condition.

The ground floor opens onto a generous entrance hall with original Minton tile floor, a double reception of 38 m² (front sitting room and rear dining room interconnected enfilade) and a 2017 side-return kitchen extension that delivers a 32 m² family-kitchen-dining at the rear. Bi-fold doors open onto a 60 m² south-facing rear garden, landscaped with mature ferns, a lawn for children and a small stone patio for dining.

The first floor accommodates the principal bedroom (en-suite shower room with bath, dressing area), two further double bedrooms and a family bathroom in honed travertine. The second floor accommodates a fourth bedroom suite (en-suite, study area) under restored eaves.

The property is freehold; EPC C; gas central heating with new boiler 2023; loft insulation 2022. The owners have lived here for fifteen years.

Hampstead Heath railway station is six minutes on foot, delivering King's Cross in twelve. Hampstead Underground (Northern) is eight minutes on foot. Highly regarded primary schools are within walking distance.

london.title: Cheyne Walk: river-front five-bed townhouse
london.description_short: Five-bedroom Grade II-listed Georgian townhouse on Cheyne Walk, with river views, private garden and discreet 2022 restoration.
london.description_long:
On the most photographed stretch of Cheyne Walk, this Grade II-listed Georgian townhouse of 360 m² has just emerged from a three-year restoration led by a recognised conservation studio. The exterior facade and original sash windows have been restored to listing-grade standard; the interior balances museum-quality detailing with a discreet, fully contemporary infrastructure.

The ground floor opens onto a stone-floored entrance hall with original cornicing, a formal sitting room of 42 m² overlooking the Thames and a separate library that faces the rear garden. The kitchen-dining occupies the lower-ground floor, opening through french doors onto a 70 m² private garden landscaped with mature magnolia.

The first floor accommodates the formal drawing room (with full-height river-facing windows and a marble fireplace), plus a study and a guest cloakroom. The second floor accommodates the principal bedroom suite (river view, dressing room, en-suite bathroom in book-matched onyx). The third and fourth floors accommodate four further bedrooms, each en-suite.

A lower-ground wellness suite includes a heated 8-metre pool, hammam and fitness studio. A discreet two-car off-street parking arrangement is included.

The King's Road, the Royal Hospital and Chelsea Embankment are all within a five-minute walk. Sloane Square Underground (District, Circle) is twelve minutes on foot.

london.title: Mayfair: trophy penthouse on Grosvenor Square
london.description_short: Trophy penthouse of 470 m² on Grosvenor Square, with 110 m² of wrap-around terraces, private lift and 24-hour concierge.
london.description_long:
On the top two floors of a celebrated 1930s mansion block on the west side of Grosvenor Square, this trophy penthouse offers 470 m² of internal space, 110 m² of wrap-around terraces and an unbroken view across the gardens of Grosvenor Square to the rooflines of Berkeley Square and Hyde Park beyond.

The penthouse was acquired by the current owner in 2019 and re-imagined by a leading London designer with a brief that delivered a discreet, museum-grade interior across four reception spaces, a state kitchen and five bedroom suites.

The ground level of the penthouse opens through a private lift onto a 28 m² entrance gallery, with library, formal drawing room of 60 m² and a separate dining room. The kitchen, by an Italian boutique maker, is finished in matt lacquer and book-matched Calacatta marble; the breakfast room opens through retractable glazing onto the south terrace.

The upper level accommodates the principal bedroom suite (a dedicated 90 m² wing comprising a private sitting room, double dressing rooms and a marble bathroom with private terrace), plus four further bedroom suites.

The building offers 24-hour concierge, valet parking and a residents-only restaurant on the ground floor. A defining piece of inventory for the international buyer who values a primary trophy address.
